newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strike seen disrupting Channel traffic on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Strike seen disrupting Channel traffic on Wednesday.

text.p: A strike call by Eurotunnel unions is expected to disrupt freight traffic through the Channel Tunnel on Wednesday, but Eurostar traffic will not be affected, union and company officials said on Tuesday.
A union source said the call to strike from Wednesday afternoon through the evening would be widely observed by several categories of workers, including conductors.
The source said French conductors would board the trains but not operate them to prevent the management from calling in British staff who are not on strike.
Eurotunnel's French unions said no decision has been made whether to call for labour action beyond Wednesday.
They accuse the management of ignoring their grievances over salaries and working hours.
The strike call is the first major action by the Eurotunnel unions which had limited their frustration to a two-hour labour stoppage prior to a fire in the subsea tunnel last November.
Eurotunnel has scheduled a meeting with unions for July 29.
It estimates 8,000 cars are counting on the freight service on Wednesday.
Eurotunnel employs just over 3,000 staff, including 1,600 French workers.
